Exactly — and that’s the irony. The moment EF gets in the way, people drop down to raw SQL anyway. At that point, what value is EF adding besides extra memory overhead and slower startup?

But I feels Dapper has that thing from the start: you write the SQL you want, no ORM surprises, no Include shits, and no hidden performance costs. EF supporting raw SQL is basically admitting its own limitations. isn't it?
